newsitem.title: ROMANIA: FOCUS - Romania PM sees July inflation under 2 pct.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Romania PM sees July inflation under 2 pct.

text.p: Romania's government, wary of a visiting IMF Mission, on Tuesday predicted monthly inflation would fall to a 1997-low of under two percent this month and said it was evidence reforms were working.

A government statement said Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea told trade unions inflation would fall below two percent from 2.3 percent in June and a record high of more than 30 percent in March after prices were liberalised.

"As far as macro-stabilisation is concerned a positive development has been recorded under the (reform) programme, with inflation of less than two percent in July," the statement quoted Ciorbea as saying.

Ciorbea also pointed to sharply increased foreign exchange reserves, first announced this month by the central bank. Officials predict reserves, which stood at $2 billion in mid-July, would rise to $4 billion by the end of the year.

An Internatioinal Monetary Fund mission is in Romania to determine whether the centrist government has met requirements for the disbursement of the second of five $86 million tranches of a $430 million standby credit approved in April.

The mission, due to remain in Bucharest until next week, has yet to comment on the government's programme in reducing inflation, proceeding with stalled privatisation and closing down inefficient farms and industries.

The government is examining a revised budget during the mission's talks, particularly new inflation figures, allocations for ministerial spending and firmer targets for dismantling state-run enterprises.
No details of the revision have been made public.
It is also holding a series of meetings with trade unionists to allay fears of mass job cuts in restructuring.
Industry and Trade Minister Calin Popescu Tariceanu says the government will keep to its target of reducing the budget deficit to 4.5 percent of gross domestic product from last year's 5.8 percent.

He told the official Rompres news agency on Tuesday that all ministries would have their allocations cut "both in social and other spheres." He also said there had been a shortfall in expected budget revenue equivalent to $ 1.52 billion.
The budget's original inflation target of 90 percent for 1997 was put beyond reach by price jumps earlier this year.
That has since been adjusted to 110-120 percent, but most economists say a figure of 150 percent is more realistic, with price rises of 101.2 percent recorded since December.
Romania's economy is plagued by spiralling arrears between companies. Ministers have also complained that slow progress in privatisation has also denied the public purse of funds.
But government ministers, particularly in the health and welfare sectors, have made plain they would defend their budget allocations against plans for cutbacks to meet IMF targets.
